title: Discrete-Laplace custom family for brms (location 0, free scale) — dlaplace1
text: Returns brms custom family discrete Laplace distribution, location fixed 0, discretised continuous Laplace(0, b) via CDF differencing: P(Z=z) = F(z+0.5) - F(z-0.5). One parameter, sigma (link = "log"), SD; mean always zero. Unlike skellam1/ skellam2, PMF CCDF closed-form (double_exponential_lcdf-based – Stan's name Laplace distribution – Bessel function, large-argument branch iteration cap needed). Use brm() call : brm(y ~ ..., family = dlaplace1(), stanvars = dlaplace1_stanvars(), data = ...)

title: Discrete-Laplace custom family for brms (location 0, free scale) — dlaplace1
text: Naming note. forced naming skellam1(): brms::custom_family() requires dpar literally named "mu"; represents sigma (SD), mean. See skellam1() Details full rationale. sigma--b conversion. Stan's double_exponential_lcdf expects continuous Laplace's scale parameter, b. Var(Laplace(0,b)) = 2*b^2, SD = b*sqrt(2); treating sigma exactly SD (discretisation perturbs true discrete variance slightly, keeps sigma scale three families) gives b = sigma / sqrt(2), computed first dlaplace1_lpmf dlaplace1_lccdf. Validation note. extraDistr::ddlaplace() implements different discrete Laplace — scale argument actually decay probability p exact closed form P(z) = (1-p)/(1+p) * p^|z|, continuous-Laplace b — confirmed numerically match family's CDF-differenced PMF (e.g. b=3, p=exp(-1/3): P(0) = 0.1535 vs 0.1651 ). package's tests validate hand-derived CDF-difference R reference instead — documented fallback package reference applicable.

title: Asymmetric Skellam custom family for brms — skellam2
text: Naming note. brms::custom_family() disallows underscores dpars (stop2("Dots underscores allowed 'dpars'.")), second parameter spelled sigmaexcess, sigma_excess package's design notes Stan code comments — two names refer quantity. Constraint algebra — corrected original design. natural-seeming construction sigma = sqrt(mu^2 + sigmaexcess^2) (Pythagorean mu sigmaexcess) guarantees sigma >= |mu|. condition Skellam validity actually needs. theta1 = (sigma^2 + mu) / 2 theta2 = (sigma^2 - mu) / 2 (theta1 + theta2 = sigma^2 theta1 - theta2 = mu), theta1, theta2 >= 0 requires sigma^2 >= |mu| — .e. Var >= |mean|, genuine Skellam constraint (sum two nonnegative Poisson rates always >= difference's absolute value). sigma >= |mu| sigma^2 >= |mu| coincide |mu| >= 1; |mu| < 1 diverge, sigma = sqrt(mu^2 + sigmaexcess^2) can produce negative theta1 theta2 — confirmed numerically, e.g. mu = 0.5, sigmaexcess = 0 gives sigma = 0.5, theta2 = -0.125. package instead uses: sigma^2 = |mu| + sigmaexcess^2 guarantees sigma^2 >= |mu| directly (right-hand side |mu| plus nonnegative term), every mu every sigmaexcess >= 0, equality (minimal-spread boundary) sigmaexcess = 0. theta1 theta2 sums nonnegative terms (verify: mu >= 0, theta1 = mu + sigmaexcess^2/2 >= 0 theta2 = sigmaexcess^2/2 >= 0; mu < 0, roles swap) — strictly positive whenever sigmaexcess > 0, log link guarantees finite linear predictor. mu = 0, reduces exactly skellam1's symmetric family (sigma = sigmaexcess, theta1 = theta2 = sigmaexcess^2 / 2). Generated-quantities note. family expose mu, sigma, sigma^2, theta1, theta2 via Stan generated quantities block. Confirmed via make_stancode(): brms declares custom family's per-observation dpar vectors (mu, sigmaexcess ) local variables inside generated model's model block, transformed parameters — Stan-scope generated quantities, regardless loop = TRUE/FALSE. Reconstructing brms's internal linear-predictor variable names (Xc, b, Intercept, ...) work simple fixed-effects-formulas, breaking silently anything random effects splines. skellam2_dpars() () reports five quantities R instead, via brms::get_dpar() — works formula.

title: skellambrms 0.3.1
text: Fixed posterior_predict_<family>() six families: previously ignored trunc()/resp_trunc() bounds entirely, drawing untruncated distribution returning verbatim (confirmed produce --bound draws, e.g. posterior_predict_dnorm2() returning values well lb = -14 bound). Now performs correct inverse-CDF sampling within truncation bounds, reusing family’s already-validated log-CCDF math (transcribed R new internal R/truncation.R) rather rejection sampling, confirmed empirically slow/low-acceptance tight bounds — especially costly skellam2(), whose per-evaluation cost (iterative Bessel-function tail-sum) comparatively high. Fixed posterior_epred_<family>() six families: previously returned untruncated mean (mu, 0 skellam1()/ dlaplace1()/dnorm1()) even truncation bound tight enough meaningfully shift conditional expectation, warning. Now computes correct truncated conditional expectation via deterministic numerical summation truncated PMF — Monte Carlo, result exact documented tolerance fully reproducible. Known limitation surfaced (introduced) fix: brms::posterior_epred() — anything built , including fitted() conditional_effects() — errors truncated fit custom family, six families , currently installed brms. brms limitation: internal dispatcher checks whether fit truncated checking whether family custom one, fallback custom family’s posterior_epred_<family>() truncated branch. Call posterior_epred_<family>(brms::prepare_predictions(fit)) directly workaround. brms::posterior_predict() unaffected works correctly truncated fits every family. See README’s “Limitations” section details.

title: skellambrms 0.3.0
text: Breaking change: skellam1() now samples sigma, SD difference (log-linked), rather underlying Skellam rate directly. mu_skellam = sigma^2 / 2 derived internally; Bessel-sum likelihood unchanged. prior previously written log(mu_skellam) translates log(sigma) = 0.5*log(2) + 0.5*log(mu_skellam) — e.g. old normal(1, 1.5) becomes normal(0.847, 0.75). reparameterisation establishes common (mean, SD-scale) convention shared every family . Added skellam2() / skellam2_stanvars() / skellam2_lccdf_stanvars(): asymmetric Skellam (Koopman parameterisation), free mean (mu) free sigmaexcess (sigma^2 = |mu| + sigmaexcess^2, guaranteeing Skellam validity every mu sigmaexcess >= 0 — corrected constraint relative originally-specified sigma = sqrt(mu^2 + sigmaexcess^2), guarantees weaker sigma >= |mu| admits invalid (negative-rate) parameter combinations |mu| < 1). Reduces exactly skellam1() mu = 0. Added dlaplace1() / dlaplace1_stanvars() / dlaplace1_lccdf_stanvars(): discrete Laplace distribution (location fixed 0, free sigma), discretised continuous Laplace via CDF differencing. Added dlaplace2() / dlaplace2_stanvars() / dlaplace2_lccdf_stanvars(): free-location/free-scale discrete Laplace, constraint coupling mu sigma — deliberate structural contrast skellam2(), comparing models bias spread structurally coupled ones vary independently. Added dnorm1() / dnorm1_stanvars() / dnorm1_lccdf_stanvars(): discrete normal distribution (location fixed 0, free sigma), via CDF-differencing pattern dlaplace1(). Added dnorm2() / dnorm2_stanvars() / dnorm2_lccdf_stanvars(): free-location/free-scale discrete normal, structurally analogous dlaplace2(). Fixed numerical-stability issue affecting skellam1_lccdf_stanvars() skellam2_lccdf_stanvars()’s normal-approximation branch, dnorm1/dnorm2’s _lpmf/_lccdf: Stan’s built-normal_lccdf safe call directly context. documented Stan limitation, guess — Stan Functions Reference states normal_lccdf underflows -inf (y-mu)/sigma > ~8.25, stan-dev/math#1985 confirms normal_lccdf (unlike normal_lcdf) never updated accurate Mills-ratio approximation. Fixed via exact erfc()-based closed form throughout, confirmed match trusted R reference machine precision 30+ SDs. Fixed Stan-compiler portability bug: skellam2_lpmf/skellam2_lccdf used fabs(), compiles rstan’s bundled Stan version valid identifier cmdstanr’s (use abs(), type-generic already used elsewhere functions). Added cmdstanr Suggests (previously rstan declared, R CMD check’s isolated test environment see already-installed cmdstanr).
